title: IELTS Academic Vol 7 - Reading Test 1 - Passage 1
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 1

Carnivorous plant

The naturalist and author of Origin of Species, Charles Darwin, was fascinated by carnivorous plants. In 1860, soon after he came across his first carnivorous plant - the sundew, Drosera - he wrote, ‘I care more about Drosera than the origin of all the species in the world.’ ... Yet sundews, he observed, ignored raindrops. To react to such a false alarm, he reasoned, would obviously be a great evil to the plant.

Darwin expanded his studies... He showed that when one of its leaves snapped shut, it formed itself into a temporary ‘stomach’, secreting enzymes that could dissolve the prey.

Today, biologists using 21st-century tools... Alexander Volkov, a plant physiologist... declares, ‘is an electrical plant.’

When an insect brushes against a hair on the leaf of a Venus flytrap... Volkov’s experiments reveal that the electric charge travels down fluid-filled tunnels in a leaf, which opens up pores in cell membranes.

The bladderwort plant has an equally sophisticated way... The cells in the bladder then begin to pump water out again, creating a new vacuum. Some of the largest have pitchers up to 30cm deep and can consume whole frogs unlucky enough to fall into them.

when scientists feed pitcher plants extra bugs, the plants get bigger. Carnivorous plants, however, take nitrogen and phosphorus from the flesh in order to build light-harvesting enzymes.

A pitcher or a flytrap is not very good at photosynthesis because, unlike plants with ordinary leaves, they do not have flat solar panels that can absorb lots of sunlight. The poor soil of bogs and swamps, where many carnivorous plants grow, offers little nitrogen and phosphorus... Also, bogs are often flooded with sunshine, so even an inefficient carnivorous plant can carry out enough photosynthesis to survive.

Chemical fertilizers used in agriculture and pollution from power plants are adding extra nitrogen to many bogs in North America. The black market trade in exotic carnivorous plants is strong. The suppression of wildfires by government agencies allows other plants to grow quickly and outcompete the Venus flytraps.
